payload.name: Extract Recipients of Directly Announced Events
payload.description: When a message directly addresses a named person and announces a personal event or news, include the addressee as the recipient in the event memory.
content: During extraction, if the speaker directly addresses a named person (e.g., 'Hey Sam!') and shares a life event or news in the same message, create an event candidate that records both the event and that the speaker told/announced it to that addressee.
If the addressee is not named but is clearly the conversation partner being informed (e.g., the other participant in the session), record that person as the recipient of the news.
Do not infer additional recipients beyond the directly addressed or clearly informed person; stop after capturing the event and its recipient.

solves: When a speaker directly tells a named person about a personal event or news, extraction often records only the event and drops the recipient, making later 'who did X tell?' questions unanswerable. This skill ensures the addressee of a direct announcement is preserved in the memory.
